topic: AI's Impact on Search and Content Strategy
headline: Getting Your Product Into ChatGPT Isn’t The Hard Part, Getting It Through Checkout Is via @sejournal, @gregjarboe
keyNotes: Orders made by AI programs searching for products have grown 15 times since January 2025 on platforms like Shopify, showing how quickly this new way of buying is expanding.
The biggest challenge isn't getting your product found by these AI programs, but making sure your online store's buying process (checkout) can handle a machine, not just a human.
Unlike humans who browse slowly, AI programs make rapid, structured requests, which can break online store systems designed to prevent automated activity or handle one continuous human visit.
A common issue is when different parts of an online store have conflicting information, like a product's price or availability; a human might overlook this, but an AI program will get stuck.
question: The article points out that many online systems are built for slow, distracted humans, not super-fast AI programs. What part of your own work or business process might create 'friction' or even break down if it suddenly had to handle interactions from a non-human, super-efficient system instead of a person?
